title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: 1Password
providers.scope_notes: Covers 1Password Business. Covers 1Password.com Business/Enterprise developer and admin credentials; Connect server and SCIM bridge are customer-hosted; CLI user sign-in is a human login and excluded except as client for service accounts.

controls.name: Service Account permission (who can create service accounts)
controls.what: Only owners/admins can create service accounts unless they grant the permission to groups or people.
controls.setting: Developer > Permissions > Service Account > Manage groups / Manage People

controls.name: Service Account Access (per vault)
controls.what: Turning off service account access on a vault removes it from all existing service accounts and blocks new grants.
controls.setting: Vault > Manage > Service Account Access toggle

controls.name: Vault permissions at creation
controls.what: Vaults and read/write/share permissions are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Service account wizard / op service-account create --vault; Connect New Token

controls.name: Revoke Token
controls.what: Revoking a service account token immediately removes its vault access.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Revoke Token

controls.name: Rotate Token
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one now, in 1 hour, or in 3 days.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Rotate Token

controls.name: --expires-in
controls.what: Sets a lifetime for a service account at creation via CLI.

no_control.what: Cannot edit an existing service account's vaults or permissions to narrow access; must revoke and recreate.

controls_unknown: Whether Business firewall rules apply to service account, Connect, Events API or Users API requests.
Whether Unlock with SSO / IdP policies affect service accounts (service_account_sso_denied is undocumented).
Whether audit log records Connect token, Events API token, SCIM credential regeneration or OAuth application create/revoke (only service account and satoken events are listed).
Whether Events API, Users API or SCIM calls themselves are logged anywhere customer-visible.
Whether a revoked Connect token or regenerated SCIM token stops working immediately.
Whether the itemusages Events API feed includes service account item access (usage reports do).

authentication.summary: A service account is a non-human 1Password user. Its token (prefix ops_) carries the account unlock key, SRP verifier and keyset and is passed as OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN to the CLI or SDKs.

federation.details: Service accounts have no email or password and are not tied to an IdP login. Docs do not say whether Unlock with SSO policies apply; the Events API lists a sign-in type service_account_sso_denied without explaining it.

ip_restriction.boundary: Business firewall rules allow/deny sign-in attempts by IP, country or anonymous IP. Docs do not say whether they apply to service account sign-ins.

lifetime.summary: No expiry unless set; CLI --expires-in at creation

renewal.expiry_basis: Token valid until revoked, deleted, or optional expiry
renewal.summary: Rotate Token issues a new token and lets the old one expire now, in 1 hour, or in 3 days.

administration.summary: Only owners/admins create service accounts by default; they can delegate to groups or people. Vault access and permissions are fixed at creation. Personal/Private/Employee/default Shared vaults are excluded.
administration.conditions: Delegated creators manage only their own service accounts; they need Manage Vault on vaults they grant.

offboard.details: A service account is its own user account for programmatic access, not tied to a team member's account.

inventory.details: 1Password.com Developer > Service accounts; owners and administrators can manage all service accounts on the team.

reads.ui: 1Password.com > Reports > Usage Report card > Create usage report > choose the service account
reads.api: POST /api/v2/itemusages (Events API; filter results on user.uuid = service account UUID)

token_format.notes: Base64-encoded JSON with email @1passwordserviceaccounts, secretKey, srpX, signInAddress.

log_sources.name: Audit log
log_sources.notes: Business; 365 days in UI; CSV export; also via Events API auditevents

log_sources.name: Usage report (service account / vault)
log_sources.notes: Business; item access with action and last access

credential_id_fields.notes: aux_info holds token name for satoken events
Service account is a user; exact representation not documented

anomaly_cues: New satoken created or rotated outside change windows
Service account reading many vaults/items (op item list fans out per vault)
Vault create by a service account

containment.steps: Developer > Service accounts > account > Revoke Token, or delete the service account; or turn off Service Account Access on affected vaults.
containment.notes: Docs: revoke immediately removes access; deleted SA token can't authenticate.

unknown: Whether individual CLI/SDK API calls are logged beyond item usage

calls.log_notes: Item access appears in usage reports (Business)

unknown: Whether whoami/list calls generate audit records

evidence.title: Use the audit log in 1Password Business
